messages.subject: suggestion: monitor() speedup
parts:
This email is just to capture a speedup suggestion for the rstan monitor() function.

For reasons previously discussed, I have switched to using plain Metropolis-Hastings MCMC written in R with an Rcpp inline likelihood function.  A simulation of 6 chains each of length 250,000 iterations (yes it is very slow to converge!) takes about 15 seconds.

However, when I pass the suitably formatted matrix into the rstan::monitor() function to analyse the results it takes about 30 minutes to produce the output - this seems a bit slow!

I recognise that this will not be a high priority given that rstan needs considerably fewer iterations to converge, but it is my understanding that you would like monitor() to be more generally used by those of us who are not able to use HMC?

Kind regards,

Sean O'Riordain
Trinity College,
Dublin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] suggestion: monitor() speedup
parts:
We're working on it --- we're moving all of the R functionality
to C++ and trying to speed it up.

You might try thinning the 250K iterations --- you're unlikely to
lose many effective samples if there's a long autocorrelation lag.

- Bob
